text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000599 bills 99215 well above expected at every complexity level, but the small set of returned records mostly supports the billed level, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"Panel acuity does not explain the excess. The 99215 share runs roughly three times the all-provider rate within every complexity stratum, including patients with zero conditions, and about a third of 99215s fall on low-complexity visits such as low back pain (C0313065), follow-up Z09 visits (C0313449) and UTI visits (C0315097, the one claim documented only at moderate). Against that, 17 of the 18 documented 99215 claims were supported, which would point toward legitimate complexity. However, records cover under 2% of claims, no audit trail was received, and documentation that matches the billed level could still be cloned or inflated. Two claims illustrate this: C0313741 is a hyperlipidemia and rash visit documented at high MDM, and C0313960 is a zero-condition back-pain 99215 that was flagged in the problems note check. The repeated-time and problems signals add mild concern, while the data-reviewed-without-lab signal is negligible. A reviewer should first pull the full notes for the low-complexity 99215 sample, especially C0313741, C0313960 and C0315097, to judge whether high MDM is credible for those presentations, then request a larger records sample and the EHR audit trail to test for templated or cloned notes."}
